items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: There was another colored gent that came in there named Buster Newman. See, he turned out to be a dance teacher, see.

ctx.x: Wouldn't you say it wasn't that many black performers going in and out the Billy Pierce Studios? It was just mostly the people that worked as assistants or playing the piano? Billy Pierce himself was a very strict man because of white performers, you know, lots of white showgirls and that. He was very strict. The school was run very strictly.

That's right. That's right. There was another colored gent that came in there named Buster Newman. See, he turned out to be a dance teacher, see. But like I say, the twins' brother, Louis Brown, he was about the only other Negro that was in there. He wasn't taking lessons. He was teaching himself. He was practicing there, you see.

Oh, yeah, and there was another gent too, Stretch Johnson. He was -- they were of these famous Cotton Club boys, you know, and that was a popular club in New York City, but it was up…
Of course, Billy was also -- excuse me -- always looking for people that could teach. See, ever since he found Buddy, he would always be looking for more Buddy Bradleys, you know.
